title: Simplifying fractions
examples: Teacher, how do I know what number to divide by?
Can you show me another example with bigger numbers?
Is finding the HCF always the easiest way?

explain.say: Today we learn to simplify fractions. This means making them smaller. We want the smallest whole numbers possible.

We use the highest common factor, or HCF. The HCF is the biggest number that divides both parts. Let us look at three over five. There is no number bigger than one that divides both three and five. So three over five is already in simplest form.

Let us try six over nine next. We look for numbers that divide both six and nine. Those numbers are one and three. Three is the highest common factor. We divide both the top and bottom by three. Six divided by three is two. Nine divided by three is three. So, six over nine becomes two over three.

Let us try ten over twenty. We need the biggest number that divides both ten and twenty. That number is ten. We divide ten by ten, which is one. We divide twenty by ten, which is two. So, ten over twenty simplifies to one over two.

faq.q: What does it mean to be in simplest form?
faq.a: It means there are no whole numbers you can divide by that will keep the fraction as a whole number. You cannot divide both the top and bottom by any number bigger than one.
asks: Is this the easiest way to write it?

faq.q: Do I always have to use the HCF?
faq.a: No, you can divide by any common factor you find. But using the HCF makes it faster because you only divide once. If you divide by a smaller number, you must keep simplifying.
asks: Must I find the biggest number?

faq.q: What if the top and bottom numbers are the same?
faq.a: If the numbers are the same, the fraction equals one. For example, five over five is one whole. You can write it as one over one.

faq.q: Is it always easier to simplify if the numbers are small?
faq.a: Yes, smaller numbers usually have fewer factors to check. However, the method stays the same no matter how big the numbers are. You just need to find the HCF.
asks: Should I worry about big numbers?

faq.a: A factor is a number that divides another number exactly, with no remainder. For example, the factors of twelve are one, two, three, four, six, and twelve.

facts: Simplifying a fraction means finding an equivalent fraction with smaller numbers.
The highest common factor is the largest number that divides both the numerator and the denominator.
Dividing the numerator and the denominator by the same number does not change the value of the fraction.
If the numerator and denominator are both prime numbers, the fraction is already in simplest form.

quiz.say: Which fraction is in its simplest form? A) 4/8 B) 5/10 C) 7/11
quiz.why: Seventy over eleven has no common factor other than one. Therefore, it cannot be simplified further.

wrong.0: This is wrong because both four and eight can be divided by two.
wrong.1: This is wrong because both five and ten can be divided by five.
wrong.2: This is wrong because both four and twelve can be divided by two.

quiz.say: What is the simplest form of twenty over forty?
quiz.why: The highest common factor of twenty and forty is twenty. Dividing both by twenty gives one over two.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you stopped dividing too early. You must continue simplifying.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you divided the top by twenty but not the bottom by twenty.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you only divided the top number and left the bottom number alone.

quiz.say: If you simplify thirty-six over seventy-two, what is the result?
quiz.why: The highest common factor is thirty-six. Dividing both thirty-six and seventy-two by thirty-six gives one over two.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you divided by six, but you could have divided by a larger number.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you divided thirty-six by itself but divided seventy-two by a much larger number.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you only divided the top number by thirty-six, not the bottom.
